concepts.name: Trigonometry and Its Applications
concepts.description: Trigonometry is the branch of mathematics that studies the relationships between the sides and angles of triangles. It has applications in engineering, architecture, astronomy, navigation, and surveying.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the purpose of trigonometry and identify its applications in real-life situations.

concepts.name: Right-Angled Triangles
concepts.description: Trigonometric ratios are defined using the sides of a right-angled triangle, namely the hypotenuse, opposite side, and adjacent side with respect to an acute angle.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the hypotenuse, opposite side, and adjacent side for a given angle in a right-angled triangle.

concepts.name: Six Trigonometric Ratios
concepts.description: The six trigonometric ratios—sine, cosine, tangent, cosecant, secant, and cotangent—describe the relationships between the sides of a right-angled triangle.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to define and calculate the six trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

concepts.name: Relationship Between Trigonometric Ratios
concepts.description: The reciprocal relationships between trigonometric ratios help simplify calculations and establish connections among the six ratios.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to derive reciprocal trigonometric ratios from given values.

concepts.name: Using Trigonometric Ratios
concepts.description: Trigonometric ratios are used to determine unknown sides or angles in right-angled triangles.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve right-angled triangle problems using appropriate trigonometric ratios.

topics.title: Trigonometric Ratios of Some Specific Angles

concepts.name: Standard Angle Values
concepts.description: The trigonometric ratios of 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, and 90° have fixed values that are frequently used in mathematical calculations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to recall and use the standard trigonometric values for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, and 90°.

concepts.name: Special Right Triangles
concepts.description: The standard trigonometric values are derived from the properties of 45°–45°–90° and 30°–60°–90° triangles.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to derive standard trigonometric values using special right triangles.

concepts.name: Application of Standard Values
concepts.description: Standard trigonometric values simplify calculations in geometry and real-life measurement problems.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve problems involving standard trigonometric values without using a calculator.

concepts.name: Fundamental Trigonometric Identity
concepts.description: The identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 is the fundamental relationship among trigonometric ratios and forms the basis for proving other identities.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to verify and apply the fundamental trigonometric identity.

concepts.name: Derived Identities
concepts.description: Other trigonometric identities are obtained by manipulating the fundamental identity and reciprocal relationships.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to derive and use basic trigonometric identities in algebraic simplification.

concepts.name: Verification of Identities
concepts.description: Verifying identities involves simplifying one side of an equation until it matches the other using known trigonometric relationships.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to verify simple trigonometric identities using standard formulas.

concepts.name: Key Concepts of Introduction to Trigonometry
concepts.description: This chapter introduces trigonometric ratios, standard angle values, and fundamental identities used to solve right-angled triangle problems.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply trigonometric ratios and identities to solve mathematical and practical problems involving right-angled triangles.
